one-check-per-line.why: expect line 1 is not quoted word for word: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file name"

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 6 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why:
I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2, 5 and 6 stay within their lines. Three conditions go further than the words require:
- **Check 3:** PASS requires "stderr names missing.jsonl". Expect line 3 only asks for an "error on stderr". Naming the file is a stricter test.
- **Check 4:** PASS requires "(empty diff)" for the whole of packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js, which is a file-scope rule. Expect line 4 only says lint(text) is unchanged.
- **Check 4:** PASS also requires that the lint tests pass, which line 4 does not ask for.

These stricter tests belonged under the Advisory heading, but they appear in PASS conditions, so the criterion is not met.

runs-as-written.why: The builder brief's commands run as written: the files exist, and `npm test` and `node --test` match the package scripts. The verifier brief does not. It defines BIN as the relative path `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js`, creates a.jsonl, bad.jsonl and the other fixtures in a separate scratch dir, then runs `node BIN a.jsonl bad.jsonl ...` and expects bare prefixes like `bad.jsonl:2: ...`. From the repo root the fixture files don't exist; from the scratch dir the relative BIN path doesn't exist. So Checks 1–3 can't run as written without the verifier rewriting the path. The other commands are valid: `npm ci` (lockfile present), git diff/merge-base, `node --test` on lint.test.js, and the gh calls with a PR placeholder.

catches-traps.why:
The briefs handle all four must_catch items.
(1) Verifier Check 3 runs `node BIN a.jsonl missing.jsonl bad2.jsonl` and passes only if it exits 2, still prints `bad2.jsonl:1: ...` on stdout and stderr names missing.jsonl. So the missing file and the bad row are tested in the same run.
(2) Check 4 runs `git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/<base>) HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` and passes only on an empty diff. That compares the file against the base commit.
(3) Builder step 4 says "Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md" with the multi-file usage, `-` for stdin and the exit codes.
(4) Check 6 reads the PR body and headRefOid through `gh pr view`, checks for the exact Closes line, and requires "the `test` workflow run for the head commit concluded success". That reads GitHub at the PR head.

avoids-must-not.why: Every behaviour check (1–3) runs the binary, so must_not item 2 is avoided. Item 1 is broken, though. Check 3's PASS condition requires that "stderr names missing.jsonl". Expect line 3 only asks for an "error on stderr", so an unreadable-file error that doesn't name the file would meet the line but fail the check. That is a stderr-content rule stricter than the line. Check 4 is also stricter than it needs to be. It requires "no change to the lint function (empty diff)" of the whole src/index.js file, while line 4 only says lint(text) is unchanged, so any other edit to that file would fail. The builder brief's exact stderr message is a build step, not a PASS/FAIL condition, so it doesn't count against item 1. The verifier's stderr requirement does, so the criterion fails.

methods-private.why: Step 3 of the builder brief repeats the verifier's own probes and PASS conditions instead of just asking for tests. It asks for "a missing file among good ones, including one with a bad row after the missing one (exit 2, stderr names the missing file, other files' bad rows still on stdout)". That mirrors Check 3's `a.jsonl missing.jsonl bad2.jsonl` run and its PASS condition "still prints bad2.jsonl:1 … stderr names missing.jsonl". "Assert output order follows argument order when two files are bad" matches Check 1's two-bad-file ordering probe. "Only that file's rows printed" matches Check 1's "nothing printed for clean files". Step 2's rule that a second `-` exits "without reading stdin (so it never blocks)" mirrors the verifier's `- -` timeout probe and Advisory. These go beyond the expect lines and pass checker methods to the builder.
